purpose: Strong direct complete-test generation baseline using the same public issue and original repository source; not a novelty claim.

generation_policy.ordering: sorted trial names; one non-retriable request per prepared trial

semantic_policy.ordering: original proposal ranks round robin over sorted trial names
semantic_policy.unknown: not executed; not an invalid-test judgment

comparative_limits: At most four editable original anchors per trial; complete contexts can contain extra original control tests.
The 24000-byte issue API catalog shares the 96000-byte budget with complete seed contexts.
Body-only generation retains registration, signatures, decorators and imports.
Original issue descriptions already contain rich semantic targets; these contracts are also available to this direct baseline.
Python requires complete AST value transport; Go and TypeScript retain the existing syntax transport and its documented limits.
Source selection, budget omissions and missing contracts limit a negative result. It cannot establish superiority over unrestricted direct models.

R20 includes historical failure candidates and historical model/native evidence; R18 only uses original repository inputs and one generation call per trial. Final detection counts alone cannot establish an equal-input equal-budget causal comparison.

validation.scope: Core/driver/native-transport tests; root inspected source cohort, request ancestry, proposal ordering and complete generation ledger.

interpretation: A negative result can arise from anchor/context/import/budget limits. Do not claim the structured methods beat unrestricted LLM generation. Every generated proposal needs fresh independent full-test model review, controlled native execution, and final source-based audit.
